obligations.note: The new integration 'payment-advice' uses https://advice.fernbrook.example/v1, satisfying the TLS requirement. The control test test_integrations_use_tls passed in CI.

The new 'payment-advice' entry in asset-inventory.json has an empty owner field ('owner': ''), violating the requirement that every integration be listed 'with an owner and a data classification.' The control test test_integrations_are_inventoried confirms the failure.
Ticket CHG-24697 is approved by change_manager erik.brandt, and its components (payments.controls-data, payments.integrations) cover both changed paths (asset-inventory.json and integrations.py).

Mara Costa (mara.costa@fernbrook.example) holds the change_approver role for payments and is not the author (Sofia Santos); her code_review approval on the correct commit satisfies independent approval.
There is a single commit and all three approvals (code_review, security_review, control_owner) reference that exact commit SHA fa3a7a35, so no later commit voids any approval.

The CI run on the final commit reports 2 test failures: test_integrations_are_inventoried and test_inventory_entries_have_owner_and_classification. The obligation requires the full suite to pass; it does not.
integrations.py is marked security_sensitive in components.json; a security_review approval from Kofi Mensah (security_reviewer, platform-security) on the correct commit satisfies the requirement.
The change touches controls/payments/asset-inventory.json (a protected path); Bao Tran (control_owner, controls-office, outside the author's payments-eng team) approved on the correct commit.
None of the files covered by the acceptance ledger entries (payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, mortgage Approvals.java/Underwriting.java) are modified by this change, so no prior evidence lapses.

summary: The change adds a new 'payment-advice' outbound integration to the payments integrations registry and asset inventory. Two obligations are violated: (1) INV-1 — the inventory entry has an empty owner field, failing the requirement that every integration be listed with an owner and a data classification; (2) CHG-4 — the CI run on the final commit shows 2 test failures (test_integrations_are_inventoried and test_inventory_entries_have_owner_and_classification), so the suite is not green. All process approvals (ticket, independent code review, security review, control-owner) are properly in place, and the new URL correctly uses HTTPS (ENC-2), but the missing owner and the failing tests are dispositive grounds for rejection.
